blocks.text: Setting up Google Sheets for onboarding on Mac

Google Sheets is a web-based app. It does not have a native Mac installer. You can still make it feel like a desktop app by using the Progressive Web App feature in Google Chrome. Open sheets.google.com in Chrome. Click the three-dot menu at the top right. Select Cast, Save, and Share. Click Install page as app. This places a shortcut in your Applications folder and lets you open Sheets in its own window.
Google Sheets tips for customer onboarding managers

Onboarding managers often face information asymmetry during the sales-to-CS handoff. Use your spreadsheet to log every milestone. Create a column for Customer Name, Status, Kickoff Date, and Next Action. Use Data Validation to create dropdown menus for status updates like Pending, In Progress, and Completed. This keeps your data consistent and prevents manual entry errors.

items: Freeze your top row so you always see headers while scrolling through large client lists.
Use Conditional Formatting to highlight rows where the status is set to Delayed.
Apply filters to quickly sort your active accounts by the next scheduled action date.
Use the ⌘ + ⇧ + H shortcut to find and replace text across your entire sheet.

blocks.text: Managing high volumes of customer data

You might manage dozens of accounts. Google Sheets supports up to 20 million cells. Avoid putting too much data in one sheet if you notice lag. Break your work into separate tabs by month or by region. Use the ⌥ + / shortcut to open the tool finder if you forget where a feature is. This saves you from clicking through menus.

items: Keeping multiple Google accounts signed in at once. This often causes permission errors.
Manually typing dates instead of using the date picker. This breaks sorting.
Ignoring the revision history. If a teammate accidentally deletes a row, you can restore it via File > Version history > See version history.

blocks.text: Keyboard shortcuts are your best friend on a Mac. Press ⌘ + / at any time to see the full list of shortcuts inside the app. For hiding rows you do not need to see right now, use ⌘ + ⌥ + 9. To hide columns, use ⌘ + ⌥ + 0. These small actions add up when you spend your whole day in spreadsheets.

faq.question: Is there a real Google Sheets app for Mac?
faq.answer: No. Google Sheets is a web application. You can create a desktop shortcut using Chrome's install feature to give it a dedicated window.

faq.question: How do I see all keyboard shortcuts in Google Sheets?
faq.answer: Press ⌘ + / while you have a sheet open to view the complete list of available shortcuts.

faq.question: Why is my Google Sheet lagging?
faq.answer: You may have reached a high cell count or have too many active collaborators. Consider splitting your data into multiple sheets or tabs.
